title: Keep a few, cull the rest
question: You asked for a way to save the ones you want and clear the others. Does this gesture read -- pin a row, press SPARE, repeat, then press CULL REST once? And is the count on the button enough warning for a destructive verb with no undo?
context_md:
The lists are `F1` (or PLANTS) then **LIST EVERY PLANT**, and `F2` (or ANTS) then **LIST EVERY ANIMAL** -- they hang off those pages because the bar has no room for a seventh chip.

New on both tables: **SPARE** beside CULL on the pinned row (it toggles, and reads SPARED while the row is on the keep list), and **CULL REST n** on the table's own header. A spared row's number draws `*3` and tints green.

The cull is graded -- the same death the brush deals -- so nothing vanishes when you press it. The rows go ROTTING and the bodies clear at the species half-life, about 3,400 ticks. That is why the count on the button matters: it is the only feedback at the moment of pressing.

Three things also got fixed on the way, all found in these pictures and by nothing else: the `*` was drawing as a **blank gap** (the font had no asterisk), the cell page was **painting over the end of BACK**, and pinning a row left the cell page reading **whatever you last clicked in the world** -- so the marker was on the ant and the panel was a plant across the bed.

items.label: three spared
items.caption: Rows *1 *2 *3 marked and tinted; CULL REST on the header; SPARED -- 3 KEPT said back.

items.label: after CULL REST
items.caption: CULLED 12, KEPT 3. The three spared still FAR/OK, everything else ROTTING, and the button now reads CULL REST 0.

items.label: the plant list, same verbs
items.caption: Both kingdoms get the same row. This is also the page where BACK used to be cut in half by the cell page.
